title: Reservation Simulation and Escalation Playbook for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a reproducible reservation simulation and an escalation playbook for dedicated capacity requests. Scope: intake validation, capacity simulation (expected throughput, tail-latency under autoscaling policies), financial tagging, approval SLA targets, and operator escalation paths. This ticket produces an operational runbook and a lightweight simulator that product managers and solutions engineers can run during sales/commit conversations. It should reduce provisioning cycle time and avoid oversubscription of GPU pools.
background: Customers frequently ask for throughput guarantees and burst behavior for Dedicated reservations. Current approval flows are manual and lack a fast, quantitative simulation to validate whether requested reservations, autoscaling rules, and fallback policies (model variants/regions) meet the requested SLA. This leads to conservative overprovisioning or repeated back-and-forth with sales/solutions engineering.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible simulator (spreadsheet + CLI wrapper) that models request distributions, batching, KV cache hit-rate, and autoscale delay; outputs expected p95 latency and required vGPU count
An approval SLA matrix mapping reservation size and requested p95 to approvals required (sales, finance, infra), with clear thresholds
An escalation playbook with contact points (on-call, solutions engineer, infra lead) and SLA for response/resolve
Runbook published in Confluence with step-by-step intake run, simulation example, and checklist for production signoff
Two pilot reservations validated with the simulator and signed off (internal teams)

open_risks: Simulator fidelity risk: real-world tail events may not be captured by default distributions; mitigated by mandatory pilot for >20 vGPU requests
Capacity contention: concurrent canary rollouts may reduce available capacity; need interlock with deployment calendar
Cost estimation: reserved discounts vary by contract; finance must validate final cost before commit
mitigations: Require a 48-hour pilot window scheduled with Infra for all reservations >20 vGPU
Add a field in intake form to capture planned rollouts/canaries so capacity planners can flag conflicts
Include a finance sign-off step on reservations that contain premium SLAs or cross-region replication
implementation_notes: Simulator inputs: request QPS distribution (Poisson/Weibull), request size distribution (tokens), model variant latency profiles, batch efficiency (% improvement by batch size), KV cache hit rates, autoscale policy parameters
Outputs: expected vGPU-hours, projected p50/p95/p99 latencies, estimated monthly cost, recommended autoscale policy adjustments
Quickstart: run spreadsheet for 5 example workload templates (chat-short, chat-long-context, embeddings-heavy, rerank-burst, streaming-gen)
Operator checklist: intake validation -> run sim -> verify cost -> schedule pilot (if required) -> approve -> reserve capacity
